clue.text: Catch the boss in a boiled shirt?

definitions.text: Catch the boss in a boiled shirt?

parts.words: Catch the boss in a boiled shirt?
parts.note: a catch is a fastener and a boss is a raised knob or stud; the small fastening knob that holds the collar to a stiff starched dress shirt

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to trap their employer while he is wearing formal evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiled shirt is a stiff, starched formal shirt whose detachable collar was fixed with a small button; 'catch' and 'boss' both describe that button, not an arrest and an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: The item is a fastener with a knob head, so 'catch' and 'boss' both describe it, and it belongs to starched formal shirts.

clue.text: House buzzer may be stuck on here

definitions.text: House buzzer may be stuck on here

parts.words: House buzzer may be stuck on here
parts.note: the house buzzer is the common housefly, not a doorbell, and the sticky strip hung up to trap it

explanation.surface: An electric doorbell might be glued to some surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House buzzer' suggests a doorbell; it is the housefly, which gets stuck to a sticky hanging strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky paper hung in a room traps flies that land on it, so a housefly ends up stuck there.

clue.text: Promise the old man a part

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man
a role is a part played by an actor

explanation.surface: A father pledges to give someone a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released on parole gives a promise of good behaviour, the original sense of the word.

clue.text: Approve of American fashion

parts.note: read as 'give approval in the American manner', the informal Americanism used as a verb for sanctioning something

explanation.surface: Someone gives their blessing to clothing styles from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of American fashion' looks like clothing; it means 'in the American way', the informal American word for giving approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an American colloquialism that as a verb means to sanction or give the go-ahead.

clue.text: Raising the issue in more than one way

definitions.text: Raising the issue in more than one way

parts.words: Raising the issue in more than one way
parts.note: raising an issue can mean mentioning a topic, and also rearing one's issue, that is one's children

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a problem using several different approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means both a topic and offspring; the phrase means both mentioning a subject and rearing children.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both introducing a subject for discussion and rearing children, two senses of raising the issue.

clue.text: Brushed off and polished again

definitions.meaning: re- plus buffed, rubbed to a shine a second time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means snubbed, and split as re-buffed it means given another polish.

clue.text: Putting spirit into a severe beating

definitions.meaning: adding a dash of alcohol to a drink
a thrashing, as in giving someone a good hiding

explanation.definitionFit: The word means adding liquor to a drink, and informally a thrashing given to someone.

clue.text: His vessel had a full complement of mates

definitions.text: His vessel had a full complement of mates

parts.words: His vessel had a full complement of mates
parts.note: a ship's mates are officers, but here mates are breeding pairs of animals taken aboard two by two into the ark

explanation.surface: A captain boasts that his ship carried all the officers it needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mates' suggests ship's officers; it means animal pairs, every species boarding the ark two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark and filled it with a male and female of every animal.

clue.text: Well-filled vessel

parts.note: well-filled usually means amply stocked, but here it is filled from an oil well

explanation.surface: A container that is generously full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-filled' looks like 'full to the brim'; it means filled with the product of an oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: This ship carries crude petroleum pumped from wells, so its cargo is well-filled.

clue.text: Time to invoke the Muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet decides the moment has come to call on divine inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: The French experts have final remedy for this disease

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of 'the'
pros are professionals, experts

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the word remedy

explanation.surface: French specialists hold the ultimate cure for some illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansen's disease is a chronic bacterial infection of skin and nerves, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Sustain in hours of trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone must keep going through difficult times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of trouble' signals that IN and HOURS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed is to sustain, keeping someone alive and healthy with food.

clue.text: Regret holding gym lessons for money

indicators.note: one word holding another means it contains it

parts.note: to rue is to regret
PE is physical education, school gym lessons

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about paying for gym classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and Pakistan, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Not a scrap of bias

parts.note: read as 'no bias at all', but a scrap is a fight, so a contest in which there is no bias

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be entirely free of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a scrap of' looks like 'not even a little'; 'scrap' is a brawl, one free of bias.
explanation.definitionFit: An even, unbiased contest between two sides is the phrase for a scrap without favouritism.

clue.text: Cor, blow me!

parts.note: Cor and blow me look like British exclamations of surprise, but cor is the French word for horn, an instrument one blows

explanation.surface: A Cockney exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor' and 'blow me' are British cries of surprise; read literally, cor is French for horn and the horn is asking to be blown.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass instrument is called cor in French, and like any horn it is played by blowing.

clue.text: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood

definitions.text: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood

parts.words: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood
parts.note: upkeep is maintenance, but it hints at the idiom of keeping up with one's neighbours

explanation.surface: Residents who look after the local streets and gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping up with the Joneses' means trying to match the neighbours' lifestyle, so this family drives the 'upkeep' of the area.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom, this family sets the standard of living the neighbours strive to keep up with.

clue.text: Contestants tied in this event

parts.note: tied suggests finishing level, but here runners have their legs literally tied together in pairs

explanation.surface: A competition ended with the competitors level on points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied' suggests a draw; it means pairs of runners strapped together at the ankle, as at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: In this sports-day race, partners have adjacent legs bound together and run as one.

clue.text: On watch, man on board provides telescope part

parts.note: to eye is to watch
a piece is a man on a chess or draughts board

explanation.surface: A lookout on deck hands over a component of a spyglass.
explanation.definitionFit: The lens at the end you look through is a component of a telescope.

clue.text: Warn a pretty girl about a Scotsman

indicators.note: the pretty girl is placed around the Scotsman

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
mon is a Scots form of 'man'

explanation.surface: Someone cautions an attractive woman about a man from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand or caution someone firmly is to warn them.

clue.text: Top gear when going into a corner?

definitions.text: Top gear when going into a corner?

parts.words: Top gear when going into a corner?
parts.note: top gear suggests a car's highest gear on a bend, but it is headwear, worn by a pupil sent to stand in the corner

explanation.surface: A driver stays in fifth gear while taking a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' and 'corner' suggest driving; it is a hat (top gear) worn by a slow pupil made to stand in the classroom corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The conical hat was put on a slow pupil made to stand in the corner, so it is head gear.

clue.text: Untidy arrangement that would horrify Mrs Grundy

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word puts its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A messy room would shock a prim neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' rearranges UNTIDY. Mrs Grundy, from an 18th-century play, is a byword for a prudish, censorious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A prude like the stock character would be scandalised by bare bodies, so nakedness is what horrifies her.

clue.text: Time of strain?

parts.note: strain suggests stress, but a strain is a piece of music, and its time is its speed

explanation.surface: A stressful period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests a stressful period; it means a tune, whose time is its speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical speed or pace is called time, so the speed of a strain of music is meant.

clue.text: Story book is a gift

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A novel makes a fine present.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is called a gift, as in a gift for music.

clue.text: Language course after a do-it-yourself setback

indicators.note: the course is placed after the reversed letters
set back is read as turned back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone takes evening classes in a foreign tongue after a home-improvement disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: This Germanic tongue written in Hebrew script is the historical language of Ashkenazi Jews.

clue.text: Right? Yes, first time

indicators.note: first puts the word for yes ahead of the letter for right

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone checks a fact and confirms it was the first occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-month period is a measure of time.

clue.text: The peace subsequently includes the French

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it within

parts.note: since can mean subsequently, as in 'he has since left'
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A later peace treaty takes in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet or stillness, the peace of a hushed room, is an absence of noise.

clue.text: Not all are like this to me

parts.note: so can mean in this way, like this
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes that only a few people share their character.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion rather than the whole is a quantity less than everything.

clue.text: Greek Upper Chamber

definitions.meaning: relating to Attica or ancient Athens
a room at the top of a house, under the roof

explanation.definitionFit: The word means of Athens, so Greek, and also a top-floor room under the roof.

clue.text: Talk of past crimes in Egyptian capital in disorder

indicators.note: letters in disorder are jumbled into a new sequence
capital points to the initial letter of the word Egyptian

explanation.surface: A detective recounts old crimes committed in a chaotic Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' gives E from Egyptian; 'in disorder' rearranges CRIMES, IN and E. 'Egyptian capital' suggests Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall and speak about old memories is to talk of the past.
